simple: This page explains the three kinds of lights you can put on objects: point lights, spotlights, and surface lights. These local lights glow from a specific object, unlike the overall sky lighting. They let you build cozy torch-lit caves, neon cities, or spooky flashlight scenes. You can set each light's color, brightness, range, and shadows.
analogy: It is like lighting a room for a play: a bare bulb lights everything around it, a flashlight only lights where it points, and a glowing TV screen lights up whatever is in front of it.
keyPoints: `PointLight` glows equally in all directions from one point. Use it for bulbs, torches, and fireballs.
`SpotLight` shines in a cone. Use it for street lamps, flashlights, and headlights. `Angle` controls how wide the cone is, up to 180 (a full half-sphere).
`SurfaceLight` glows from a whole face of a part. Use it for screens, signs, and light panels.
`Face` on spotlights and surface lights picks which side of the part the light comes out of.
`Range` is how far the light reaches, in studs. A range of 12 lights up things up to 12 studs away.
All lights share `Color`, `Brightness`, and `Shadows`. Brightness is strongest at the center but never reaches farther than the range.
To insert a light, add it into an Attachment or a part in the Explorer. Attachments are best for a light from one exact spot.
Turn on Show Light Guides in Studio Settings to see where each light reaches.

terms.local light: A light that comes from a specific object, as opposed to global lighting from the `Lighting` service that lights the whole world.
terms.range: How far, in studs, the light reaches from its source. Outside that distance it adds no light at all.
terms.brightness: How strong the light is near its center. Turning brightness from 2 to 10 makes the lit area brighter, not bigger.
terms.cone: An ice-cream-cone shape. Spotlights shine out in this shape from their tip.
terms.apex: The pointed tip of the cone, where the spotlight's light starts.
terms.angle: How wide the light spreads. A spotlight with Angle 30 is a narrow beam; 75 is much wider.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green, and blue numbers. [255, 100, 50] is an orange.
terms.shadows: Dark areas where an object blocks the light. Turning `Shadows` on makes blocked areas dark.
terms.Face: One side of a part, like Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front, or Back.

example.title: Add an orange torch glow to a part
example.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace
example.code:
local part = script.Parent

local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
light.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 100, 50) -- warm orange
light.Brightness = 2
light.Range = 12 -- lights things up to 12 studs away
light.Shadows = true
light.Parent = part

-- Make it flicker like a real flame
while true do
	light.Brightness = 1.5 + math.random() -- between 1.5 and 2.5
	task.wait(0.1)
end
explain: We create a `PointLight` so it glows in every direction.
`Range = 12` means the light reaches 12 studs from the part.
Putting the light inside the part makes it glow from there.
The loop changes the brightness a little every 0.1 seconds, so it flickers like fire.

watchOut: Raising `Brightness` will not make a light reach farther. Raise `Range` for that.
A spotlight pointing the wrong way usually has the wrong `Face`. Change `Face` or rotate the part.
Lots of lights with shadows on can slow down weaker devices. Use only what you need.
